ingredients.name: Banana flower (banana blossom)
ingredients.notes: medium-large, cleaned (see step 1); canned banana blossom in brine can substitute -- drain and rinse well before use

ingredients.name: Turmeric powder
ingredients.notes: split between soaking water and the curry

ingredients.name: Lime
ingredients.notes: juiced; added to the soaking water to prevent browning

ingredients.name: Coconut oil
ingredients.notes: for frying the cleaned banana flower before adding to the curry

ingredients.name: Onion
ingredients.notes: sliced; some reserved for the final temper

ingredients.name: Goraka
ingredients.notes: small piece; or substitute 1 tsp tamarind juice

ingredients.name: Maldive fish flakes
ingredients.notes: optional; omit for a fully vegan curry

steps.instruction: Cleaning the banana flower is the most important and time-consuming step. Remove the dark outer maroon bracts (layers) one by one, discarding them or reserving for another use, until you reach the pale inner core. As you peel, you will find rows of small florets -- each floret has a thin papery sheath and a small stamen. Remove both from each floret before chopping (the stamen and sheath can cause bitterness if left in). Chop the pale inner layers and cleaned florets finely. Immediately drop chopped pieces into a bowl of water with lime juice and a pinch of turmeric to prevent browning.
Drain the banana flower, then squeeze out as much water as possible using your hands. Season with a little turmeric and salt.

Heat the coconut oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Fry the banana flower pieces in the oil for 4-5 minutes until lightly golden and slightly dried out. Remove and set aside. This frying step reduces bitterness and improves texture significantly.

In the same pan, add the mustard seeds and let them splutter. Add the onion, garlic, curry leaves, pandan leaf, cinnamon, cardamom (if using), and green chillies. Saute until the onion softens, about 3 minutes.
Add the chilli powder and curry powder, stir briefly. Add the goraka (or tamarind juice) and Maldive fish flakes (if using) and mix through.
Add the fried banana flower back to the pan. Pour in the thin coconut milk and salt. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook for 12-15 minutes until the banana flower is tender.
Pour in the thick coconut milk. Stir and simmer gently uncovered for 3-5 minutes until the gravy thickens. Taste and adjust salt. Serve hot with rice.

source_site: islandsmile.org, cross-checked against foodcnr.com, pulse.lk (Aunty D), veganphysicist.com, exploresrilanka.lk, and infolanka.com
collection_method: scraped, cross-checked across 6+ independent sources; strong agreement on the cleaning technique and the importance of frying before adding to the gravy
notes: The cleaning process for banana flower is the single most discussed and most time-consuming part of this recipe -- removing the stamen and papery sheath from each individual floret is fiddly, and the flower releases a sticky sap that stains hands brown (wearing gloves and oiling hands beforehand is recommended). The soaking in lime-juice water prevents browning. Shallow-frying the cleaned banana flower before adding to the curry is strongly recommended by most sources as it reduces bitterness and improves texture; skipping this step produces a softer, slightly more bitter result. Canned banana blossom in brine (widely available in Asian supermarkets) is a reliable, much faster substitute -- drain and rinse thoroughly before using. The dish is sometimes described as having a texture similar to artichoke hearts once cooked.
